title: Galatasaray confirm Noa Lang thumb surgery after colliding with Anfield hoardings
content:
Galatasaray have confirmed that Noa Lang will have surgery in Liverpool on his right thumb after cutting it in a collision with the advertising hoardings at Anfield.

The Netherlands international slid into the boards in the latter stages of the Turkish club’s Champions League 4-0 (4-1 aggregate) loss and had to be taken off on a stretcher after a six-minute delay. Lang, 26, was in considerable pain and the tip of his thumb appeared partially severed.

Galatasaray’s head coach said after the match that he was going to hospital before the club confirmed early on Thursday morning in a statement that the attacker had a “serious cut”. The statement said he would undergo an operation via their medical team “in the coming hours” before leaving the city.

Liverpool FC plan to investigate what exactly happened during the incident which caused the injury and wish Lang a full and speedy recovery.

“It’s a very big accident but it’s nothing to do with the stadium, it’s just an accident,” Liverpool captain and Netherlands team-mate Virgil van Dijk said after the game. “I spoke to him, hopefully he will be back on the pitch asap because we need him if he’s coming to the national team next week.”

The Super Lig club also confirmed that Victor Osimhen sustained a right arm fracture after a blow in the first half and may face surgery. The Nigeria forward was taken off at half time and replaced by Leroy Sane “due to the risk of breaking his arm” and the side said they will conduct further evaluations before potentially deciding on an operation.

Lang has been a regular in Galatasaray’s starting line-up since moving on loan from Napoli in January. Despite 11 of his 18 Serie A appearances coming from the substitutes bench, he also played in two of the Netherlands’ World Cup qualifiers last year.

Osimhen, 27, has scored 19 goals in all competitions over 29 appearances for Galatasaray this season, after his loan move from Napoli was made permanent in the summer.
